correctness.rationale: Complete proof: nonzero-edge connected blocks have at most one kernel dimension by invertible offdiagonal row propagation. The continuant recurrence gives p_i=(1−(−1/q)^i)/(q+1), hence exact connected-block weights; unique zero-edge segmentation and a geometric-series sum yield the rational all-rank generating function. At t=1 the dominant pole is q² and the subdominant is −(q−1), so the analytic moment-generating function yields mean 1/(q²+q−1), strictly positive variance 1/δ−(q²−q+1)/δ³ and CLT. Independent Gaussian elimination exhaustively checked 9,887 matrices over five finite fields, including GF(4); finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact complete corank polynomial is a naturally defined invariant of a classical sparse symmetric matrix ensemble for every field and dimension, not merely a special numeric evaluation. The linear nullity density and explicit Gaussian limit identify a structural sparse-vs-dense change invisible to the already-known determinant-only count and conditional connected path formula; the precise rank multiplicities can be used to analyze finite-field tridiagonal systems and graph-representing matrices.
